thread:
deploy-bot: Release rel-332 slice rollout to runtime-pool-a started at 2026-03-17T10:12:01Z (id=rel-332). Canary=5%.

alex: noticing increased tail latency on canary, P50 fine but P95/P99 jumping. throughput for pool-a down ~30%.
maria: confirming on graphs https://grafana/redwood/runtime - p99 ~1.2s vs baseline 80ms. kernel fallback spikes on canary nodes.
sam: any customer impact yet?
jin: support dashboard shows ~0.6% 502s for a handful of premium customers in eu-west, started ~10:16 UTC, small but climbing. CS pinged.
ops-bot: incident created (sev=P1) -> paging oncall. Incident channel: #incidents/1718004321.
alex: pausing rollout is safest immediate step. we can also flip the feature flag to stop the slice.
maria: agree. preliminary root cause: change in batching window + kernel affinity tweak in rel-332 causing microbatches to hit an unoptimized kernel path under certain sequence lengths -> fallback path thrashes.
sam: plan: 1) pause/cancel rollout 2) flip rollout flag 3) rollback to rel-331 if needed 4) route traffic to stable pool. who can flip flag?
leo-cs: @maria I can flip the FF from the console if you give me the key.
maria: flag key: `rollout/rel-332-slice`. CLI: `redwood feature toggle --key rollout/rel-332-slice --off`
jin: executing flag toggle now.
support: drafted customer note: "We're investigating increased latency/502s impacting a subset of requests in eu-west. We're mitigating and will follow up." want me to send after mitigation?
alex: oncall handoff: handing to @maria for execution and root cause, timeline updates.
incident-bot: oncall handoff recorded: primary alex -> maria at 2026-03-17T10:23:10Z.
alex: paused canary: `redwood rollout pause rel-332` -> confirmed paused.
maria: flag turned off, verifying traffic drain from slice.
ops-bot: scaling notice: stable pool scaled +4 nodes to absorb traffic; routing adjustments applied.
alex: kernel fallback counts dropping, p99 trending back toward baseline (now ~120ms).
sam: preparing rollback to rel-331 for the slice.
maria: rollback command used: `redwood rollout revert --id rel-332 --target rel-331`
jin: rollback executed at 2026-03-17T10:31:45Z, monitoring metrics.
```
# logs excerpt
[10:31:46] rollback: started rel-332 -> rel-331 on pool-a-slice-B
[10:32:03] healthcheck: 200 OK on new instances
[10:32:30] kernel_fallbacks: normalized
```

support: CS notified affected customers with interim note. two customers requested timeline; escalated to enterprise success.
alex: observed throughput recovered to baseline, error rate returned to normal within ~12 minutes of rollback.
maria: capture: peak impact window ~10:16-10:28 UTC, ~12 minutes where small subset saw 5xx. approximate affected request ratio 0.5-0.8% depending on region.
jin: collecting logs/evts for postmortem (kernel traces, batching window histograms, rollout artifacts).
ops-bot: remediation checklist applied: pause-rollout, FF-off, rollback, scale-stable, CS notify.
incident-bot: incident status -> mitigated. will convert to postmortem. tags: deploy-regression,kernel-fallback,batching.
sam: please add owners: maria (engineer lead), alex (oncall), jin (support logs), leo-cs (customer comms). postmortem due EOD tomorrow.
incident-bot: incident closed for paging at 2026-03-17T10:49:35Z.

maria: quick note for postmortem: stop-gap: re-enable stricter kernel-affinity checks in CI, add canary extra-slowpath smoke, and add alert for cross-pool fallback rate >0.1%.
alex: adding a runbook step: if P99>500ms and fallback_count rising, immediately pause rollout and flip `rollout/*` flags.
incident-bot: archival: this thread saved to /incidents/rel-332-rollout."
